claim: CAMP trains 4096 parallel agents in Isaac Gym on an NVIDIA RTX 4060Ti GPU for approximately 7 hours to learn multi-skill quadruped locomotion.
stance_target: AMP training budgets on consumer GPU hardware
scope_conditions: CAMP multi-skill AMP, Unitree Go2/A1 quadruped, single consumer GPU
quoted_support: 'We trained 4096 parallel agents using the Isaac Gym simulator. The policy was trained with million simulated time steps. Training is conducted on an NVIDIA RTX 4060Ti GPU and takes approximately 7 hours.'

claim: CAMP's step count is reported as '[X] million simulated time steps' where the number was not captured in the HTML rendering — likely 1000M (1B) steps based on context.
quoted_support: 'The policy was trained with million simulated time steps.' (Number before 'million' appears truncated in HTML extraction.)

claim: CAMP's motion reference dataset is generated from model-based controller (not mocap), consisting of forward/backward/lateral/turning/composite trajectories with 4 gait types, each clip ~4 seconds.
stance_target: AMP demo dataset size and generation method
quoted_support: 'We generate quadrupedal locomotion sequences on flat terrain using a model-based control approach, without relying on real-world motion capture data... Our dataset comprises various locomotion trajectories... with each trajectory lasting approximately 4 seconds.'

claim: CAMP uses a conditional AMP discriminator with 43-dimensional state (joint positions/velocities, base linear/angular velocity, base height, foot positions) conditioned on skill latent variable z.
stance_target: AMP discriminator state space design for multi-skill learning
quoted_support: 'Each state s_t^CAMP in R^43 comprises joint positions, joint velocities, base linear velocity, base angular velocity, base height, and foot positions.'

claim: CAMP's network architecture: Actor and Critic both use [512,256,128] MLP; conditional AMP discriminator uses [1024,512] MLP; skill discriminator uses [512,256] MLP.
stance_target: AMP policy and discriminator network sizes for legged locomotion

claim: CAMP reward structure: task reward weight 1.5 (velocity x) + 0.75 (yaw), style reward weight 1.0, skill reward weight 0.3; no contact or airborne penalties mentioned.
stance_target: AMP reward weighting for natural locomotion without explicit contact penalties
quoted_support: Table II: 'r_task: exp(-||v_xy_cmd - v_xy||/0.15) weight 1.5, exp(-||omega_z_cmd - omega_z||/0.15) weight 0.75; r_style weight 1.0; r_skill weight 0.3'

claim: CAMP ablation studies compare all variants using 15,000 PPO update steps — but this is the ablation budget, not the full training budget.
quoted_support: 'Each policy is trained for 15,000 steps, and all randomization settings remain consistent during training.'

claim: CAMP achieves 91.23% and 91.38% average joint trajectory tracking accuracy on real hardware (Unitree Go2), deployed directly without additional parameter tuning.
stance_target: AMP sim-to-real transfer quality for quadruped locomotion
scope_conditions: CAMP on Unitree Go2 real robot, 10s continuous skill switching
quoted_support: 'the average tracking accuracy of the joint trajectories reaches 91.23% and 91.38%, respectively'
